title: Bleeding Edge Alert! Generative Adversarial Networks for Recommendations

cues.en: It's time for another bleeding-edge alert, where we go to the cutting edge of recommender system research.
cues.zh: 又到了前沿研究提醒，來看推薦系統研究的最前沿。

cues.en: This time we're going to talk about applying generative adversarial networks to recommender systems.
cues.zh: 這次談生成對抗網路，如何用於推薦系統。

cues.en: This is really a hot area right now as are GANs in general.
cues.zh: 目前真的很熱門，GAN 整體也是如此。

cues.en: And it's not just because they're being used for viral apps and deep fakes.
cues.zh: 不只是因為熱門應用與 Deepfake。

cues.en: It turns out you can also apply them to the problem of making recommendations with just a few twists.
cues.zh: 其實只要一些調整，就能應用到推薦問題。

cues.en: So let's revisit GANs.
cues.zh: 回顧 GAN。

cues.en: We covered this in the intro to Deep Learning Section.
cues.zh: 深度學習入門介紹過。

cues.en: But just to refresh your memory here, this is an example of using, again, to generate random images
cues.zh: 提醒一下，這是用 GAN，隨機產生

cues.en: of faces and what's going on here as we're starting with an input of random noise so that we get a randomly generated faces, and we're training a generator to try to create realistic images of faces.
cues.zh: 人臉影像的例子。從隨機雜訊輸入開始，得到隨機人臉，訓練生成器，產生逼真人臉影像。

cues.en: At the same time, we're feeding this system real faces up here at the top here.
cues.zh: 同時，也把真實人臉輸入系統上方。

cues.en: And these are all going into a discriminator that's trying to learn the difference between real images and fake images.
cues.zh: 全部送入判別器，學習真實與假影像的差異。

cues.en: So over time, these two things are in tension with each other.
cues.zh: 兩者隨時間互相抗衡。

cues.en: The generator is constantly trying to fool the discriminator into thinking that it's generated faces are real.
cues.zh: 生成器不斷欺騙判別器，讓它認為生成臉是真的。

cues.en: And at the same time, the discriminator is getting better and better at telling real faces from generated fake faces.
cues.zh: 同時，判別器越來越擅長，分辨真人臉與生成假臉。

cues.en: So so over time, if you have the same tune properly, it will become very, very good at making convincing looking faces that are actually fabricated.
cues.zh: 因此，如果調整適當，隨時間，會非常擅長製造逼真、但其實虛構的人臉。

cues.en: So how would we take this system and apply to recommender systems?
cues.zh: 如何用到推薦系統？

cues.en: Well, it's pretty straightforward, it turns out.
cues.zh: 其實相當直接。

cues.en: So first of all, we're not interested in generating pictures of faces here.
cues.zh: 首先，不再生成臉孔圖片。

cues.en: We're generating ratings.
cues.zh: 而是產生評分。

cues.en: Right.
cues.zh: 對吧？

cues.en: So instead of generating 2D images, we're going to be generating the set of user item ratings for the entire set of users and items.
cues.zh: 不產生二維影像，而是對所有使用者與項目，產生整套使用者／項目評分。

cues.en: That's what we're trying to fabricate here.
cues.zh: 這就是要製造的內容。

cues.en: And we obviously won't be feeding the discriminator.
cues.zh: 顯然，也不再向判別器輸入

cues.en: Real faces anymore will be feeding it real ratings that actually come from real ratings from real people.
cues.zh: 真實人臉，而是來自真實使用者的真實評分。

cues.en: So we're going to be trying to generate the entire set of user item ratings and feeding at the real set of actual observed user-item ratings to compare against.
cues.zh: 因此，試著產生整套使用者／項目評分，並提供實際觀察到的真實評分比較。

cues.en: So the discriminator is trying to tell real ratings from fabricated ratings for every user and item.
cues.zh: 判別器要對每位使用者與項目，區分真實與虛構評分。

cues.en: Also, we're not going to be using convolution layers for the generator and discriminator because we're not dealing with images.
cues.zh: 另外，生成器與判別器不使用卷積層，因為不是影像。

cues.en: So when people started using GANs for recommender systems, they started off by just using straight up multilayer Perceptron or Matrix Factorization techniques.
cues.zh: 人們最初用 GAN 做推薦，直接用多層感知器或矩陣分解。

cues.en: And those worked pretty well.
cues.zh: 效果相當好。

cues.en: But more recent research is actually using recurrent neural networks and GRUs, because it turns out
cues.zh: 較近期研究，改用 RNN 與 GRU，因為發現，

cues.en: that the RELU function in an RNN actually does a really good job of basically forgetting old behavior over time.
cues.zh: RNN 的 ReLU 函數，很擅長隨時間忘記舊行為。

cues.en: And this actually leads to better recommendations in their research.
cues.zh: 研究中，這能帶來更好的推薦。

cues.en: So the generator won't be using transposed conv2D layers.
cues.zh: 因此，生成器不用 Conv2DTranspose。

cues.en: They're gonna just be using straight up RNNs.
cues.zh: 而是直接用 RNN。

cues.en: And the discriminator also will be using RNNs as well instead of convolution layers.
cues.zh: 判別器也使用 RNN，取代卷積層。

cues.en: So we're replacing the topology of those networks.
cues.zh: 也就是替換網路拓樸。

cues.en: And finally, we're not going to be feeding it random noise, because our objective is not to create a randomly generated set of ratings for a random user.
cues.zh: 最後，不輸入隨機雜訊，因為不是要替隨機使用者，產生隨機評分集合。

cues.en: We want specific ratings for real people.
cues.zh: 要的是真實使用者的特定評分。

cues.en: Right.
cues.zh: 對吧？

cues.en: So we're going to be feeding this older real world ratings instead.
cues.zh: 因此，改輸入較早的真實評分。

cues.en: The idea is that we're going to pick some time, some point in time, call it T, and we're going to feed it in the ratings before that time T and you know, going forward, we're going to be trying to
cues.zh: 概念是，選某個時間點 T，輸入 T 之前的評分，再往後，試著

cues.en: generate predicted ratings after that.
cues.zh: 生成 T 之後的預測評分。

cues.en: So that's the approach taken in one paper at least.
cues.zh: 至少有一篇論文這樣做。

cues.en: So this is how a GAN might look for a recommender system.
cues.zh: 這就是推薦系統 GAN 的可能樣子。

cues.en: And you can see we just replaced the images with ratings, replace the topology of the generator and discriminator with RNNs.
cues.zh: 可以看到，影像換成評分，生成器與判別器拓樸，換成 RNN。

cues.en: And one example, and instead of feeding it random data, we're feeding it old ratings instead.
cues.zh: 這是一個例子；輸入不再隨機資料，而是舊評分。

cues.en: And it turns out it works pretty well.
cues.zh: 效果相當好。

cues.en: So if you want to go and read the original paper, here's a link to it here and how to find it.
cues.zh: 想讀原論文，這裡有連結與尋找方式。

cues.en: There is also pretty good.
cues.zh: 結果也相當好。

cues.en: Now, they did kind of cherry-pick the models they compared themselves to.
cues.zh: 不過，他們有點挑選比較模型。

cues.en: They only looked at other models that deal with TIME series data.
cues.zh: 只看處理時間序列的其他模型。

cues.en: But in those comparisons, they did really, really well.
cues.zh: 但那些比較中，表現非常好。

cues.en: It was really good.
cues.zh: 真的很好。

cues.en: So it's not just a fad.
cues.zh: 因此，不只是風潮。

cues.en: I mean, GANs are kind of the latest hotness, but in this case, they actually do a pretty good job.
cues.zh: GAN 雖是最新熱門技術，但這個例子，確實做得不錯。

cues.en: My only beef with this approach is that, as we saw earlier, GANs are incredibly resource intensive.
cues.zh: 我唯一不滿，是如前所見，GAN 極耗資源。

cues.en: So it takes a lot of computing power to do this.
cues.zh: 需要很多運算能力。

cues.en: And you can imagine if you're dealing with a large data set where you're dealing with every user item power over millions of users.
cues.zh: 想像大型資料集，數百萬使用者的每個使用者／項目配對，

cues.en: This is way, way more intensive, just trying to generate a picture of a face.
cues.zh: 比只生成一張人臉，密集得多。

cues.en: Right.
cues.zh: 對吧？

cues.en: But they did it.
cues.zh: 但他們做到了。

cues.en: They actually demonstrated doing this on the full Netflix data set as a measure themselves on that basis.
cues.zh: 確實在完整 Netflix 資料集上示範，衡量結果。

cues.en: And they also compare themselves on the subset of Netflix data using the six million Netflix data set.
cues.zh: 也以六百萬筆 Netflix 子資料集比較。

cues.en: So they've proven that this approach can work well on very sparse data situations, as well as more dense data situations as well.
cues.zh: 因此，證明不管非常稀疏，或較密集資料情況，都能有效運作。

cues.en: It's quite resilient in that way.
cues.zh: 這方面相當有韌性。

cues.en: So like I said, this is only one of many papers on GANs for recommendations.
cues.zh: 如前所說，這只是很多 GAN 推薦論文之一。

cues.en: If you do a search, you'll find several.
cues.zh: 搜尋會找到好幾篇。

cues.en: And this does kind of seem to be the direction of research these days, actually demonstrating this and a little notebook that you can actually run on your PC.
cues.zh: 這似乎是目前研究方向。不過，要在能於自己電腦執行的小 Notebook，實際展示，

cues.en: It's not going to happen.
cues.zh: 是不可能的。

cues.en: It's too complicated.
cues.zh: 太複雜。

cues.en: But you get the general idea here.
cues.zh: 但你已了解大致概念。

cues.en: If you take a GAN, swap in ratings for the images, you pretty much got the idea and it works pretty well.
cues.zh: 取得 GAN，把影像換評分，基本上就掌握概念，效果相當好。

cues.en: So that's RecGAN or using generative adversarial networks for recommendation systems in a nutshell.
cues.zh: 這就是 RecGAN，也就是生成對抗網路推薦的概要。
